title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index (August 2027), 10:00 a.m. ET — the last Tuesday, the last calendar day and the last session of August at once
source: EST: the publisher's standing rule, restated on conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 332,031 bytes -- byte-identical to the 07-27 sibling's fetch) -- "The Conference Board publishes the Consumer Confidence Index (R) at 10 a.m. ET on the last Tuesday of every month." 2027-08-31 is the last Tuesday of August 2027. The rule is verified for AUGUST specifically, 3 of 3 and every one of the three DOUBLE-SOURCED, against the publisher's own pages fetched direct 2026-09-06 and each read against its own "Source: August <year> Consumer Confidence Survey" line rather than trusted by slug: CCI-August-2022 (883,112 bytes, released 2022-08-30), CCI-August-2023 (1,254,077 bytes, 2023-08-29) and CCI-Aug-2024 (883,880 bytes, 2024-08-27) -- each the last Tuesday of its August, and each independently named IN ADVANCE by the preceding July edition's own next-release line: CCI-July-2022 "The next release is Tuesday, August 30 at 10 AM ET", CCI-July-2023 "Tuesday, August 29", CCI-July-2024 "Tuesday, August 27th". A fourth August, 2026-08-25, is live on the publisher's landing page. THE CALENDAR ARITHMETIC IS INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED BY A SECOND PUBLISHER'S POSTED FORWARD CALENDAR: fhfa.gov/data/hpi, fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 89,663 bytes), carries a "2027 HPI Release Dates" table whose twelve rows read Tuesday January 26 / February 23 / March 30 / April 27 / May 25 / June 29 / July 27 / AUGUST 31 / September 28 / October 26 / November 30 / December 28 -- identical to this chain's rule-derived last Tuesdays for all twelve months of 2027, 12 of 12, posted a year ahead by an agency publishing on the same last-Tuesday cadence. That removes the ARITHMETIC risk from this date; it says nothing about the Conference Board's intentions, which is why this stays estimate. CCI-August-2021, CCI-August-2025 and CCI-August-2026 each returned HTTP 200 while serving the current August 2026 edition under BOTH the full-month and abbreviated slug conventions, and are recorded in the ledger's probe-ref.blocked rather than counted. No August-2027 announcement exists yet, so this is the publisher's rule applied forward against a three-deep double-sourced August record and an outside publisher's matching table, rather than a posted date. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: CANONICAL FILE written by the consumer-confidence-2027-08-31 initial-research lane (2026-09-06) after reading the one prior proposal, proposals/consumer-confidence-2027-08-31.from-consumer-confidence-2027-07-27.json, which is now inert. THAT PROPOSAL FILED THIS ID AS A CONTROL AND THE CONTROL COMES BACK NULL, which is the finding. The 07-27 sibling had proved a July print is never observed clean (0 of 6, because every FOMC day one in Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct IS that month's last Tuesday, 22 of 22) and proposed August as the within-summer clean twin: same season, same publisher, clean 6 of 6. Run head to head on the identical nine-instrument pipeline (n=1,447 sessions, stockanalysis.com + CBOE, replicating the April-July siblings' clean-day table to three decimals and their 51/17 split exactly), AUGUST CB DAYS vs JULY CB DAYS IS 0 OF 9 -- smallest p QQQ 0.4233, the least significant of the five controls run. August is 0 of 9 four more ways (vs other clean CB days, other August sessions, other late-August sessions, all non-CB sessions). So the FOMC collision the whole 07-27 ledger was about is a calendar fact and not a tape fact: the sibling's structural claim survives, its practical implication does not, and this chain should stop pricing a collision. WHAT IS MEASURABLE IS THE CELL, NOT THE PRINT -- late August (22nd onward) runs 6 of 9 NARROWER than the rest of the year (n=42, XLF 0.0012, VIX 0.0027, XLY 0.0049), inside an August that is 9 of 9 narrower (n=132) and a summer block 9 of 9 narrower (n=383, confirming FT-consumer-confidence-2027-06-29-4 out of sample), while the print adds nothing to that quiet. TWO CAUTIONS THE PROPOSAL RAISED ARE BOTH CONFIRMED. August's cut-off lags are 7/9/6 days (2022-08-23, 2023-08-20, 2024-08-21) plus 9 again in 2026 -- the LONGEST in the chain against July 5/6/8, June 6/7/6, May 8/7/8, April 6/6/8 -- so borrowing July's 5-day figure would have put the 2027 cut-off three days late; project 08-22 to 08-25. And the chain's 80-threshold premise is not merely refuted but CLUSTERED IN AUGUST: sourced Augusts print Expectations 75.1 / 80.2 / 82.5, 2 of 3 above the Board's recession line, and TWO of this chain's threshold readings flipped side ON REVISION -- CCI-Aug-2024 revised July 2024's Expectations from a first-printed 78.2 up to 81.1 and wrote that "August marked the second consecutive month of the Index above 80", a year after CCI-July-2023 restated June 2023's 79.3 as exactly 80.0. The threshold is not readable off a first print at all. AUGUST ALSO SETS TWO REVISION RECORDS: CCI-August-2023 restates July's Present Situation at 153.0 against a 160.0 first print (-7.0, beating the -6.2 the 07-27 sibling called this chain's largest) and its headline at 114.0 against 117.0 (-3.0, beating -2.6). STRUCTURE OF THIS DATE: 2027-08-31 is the last Tuesday, the last calendar day AND the last trading session of August simultaneously -- true in only 2 of the 7 Augusts 2021-2027 -- and that coincidence is measurably worth nothing (month-final CB days 1 of 9 vs other CB days, 0 of 9 vs other month-final sessions, month-end itself 0 of 9). It is also the ONLY 2027 CB print in a month with no FOMC blackout: a 37-day clear-air gap runs 2027-07-29 to 2027-09-04 and this print lands on day 33 of it, with a panel that closed 6-9 days earlier and so cannot hear the final week of August. CORRIDOR: zero tracked events existed anywhere in August 2027 before this PR; two are proposed here, of which fhfa-hpi-2027-08-31 is a QUARTERLY HPI release at 9:00 ET on this print's own morning. Estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
